_note: What real parts are like, by function. The sheetset line classifies every region of a part map into one of these and sizes it here: the painting says where, the depth map says relatively how much, this file says how much is believable. Millimetres. 'out' = stands proud of the surface, 'in' = recess depth. Add a class when a new kind of part shows up; every asset after that benefits.

handle.why: fingers must fit behind a pull handle: 15-25 mm gap plus the grip

hinge.why: exposed appliance and door hinges are a knuckle a few mm proud

foot.why: levelling feet and kick bases lift the body off the floor

knob.why: see part_rules.py: 2-6 cm knobs stand out 60% of their diameter

key.why: typewriter and keyboard keys stand on stems above the deck

cornice.why: building cornices overhang the wall to shed rain

sill.why: window sills project to drip water clear of the wall

seam.why: the gap round a door or drawer: a fingernail, not a slot

vent.why: louvres and grilles: shadow, not a hole

dispenser.why: a glass must fit under the spout: a tumbler is ~9 cm across

recess.why: general pockets, handles cut into a panel, display niches

window.why: window glass sits back in a masonry wall

door_opening.why: street doors sit back in their frames

pit.why: screw heads, rivets and small holes drawn as dots: shadow only
